business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Battery-Grade Lithium Carbonate Powder

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (entered into force 1 December 2007)
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the People's Republic of China (entered into force 20 December 2015)
Convention between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 17649, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality (Act No. 11662, as amended); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Crime Proceeds (Act No. 16621, as amended); Act on Prohibition of Financing of Offenses against Public Threats; Commercial Act, Articles 18, 19, 20, 22, 23 and 54; FATF Recommendations 10, 24 and 25. For a Yuhan Hoesa private limited liability company, beneficial owner identification is conducted at the 25% shareholding or voting-rights threshold; the resulting beneficial ownership information is filed with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KOFIU) and the National Tax Service under the statutory reporting regime and is accessible to those government authorities but not to the general public.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate) issued by the competent court registry upon formation of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registry office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a licensed Korean notary public followed by a Hague Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; Apostille path only, consular legalization not used and not chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Company Register Extract, including current registration details and legal existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Commercial Registry office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a licensed Korean notary public followed by a Hague Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; Apostille path only, consular legalization not used and not chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution appointing the Representative Director and granting Power of Attorney to the foreign agent or signatory for bank account opening and trade documentation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of board minutes notarized before a licensed Korean notary public followed by a Hague Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; Apostille path only, consular legalization not used and not chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Articles of Incorporation (Articles of Association) in Korean with English translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa registered office and the Korean Commercial Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization before a licensed Korean notary public followed by a Hague Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; Apostille path only, consular legalization not used and not chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the proposed corporate account relationship and trade-finance capacity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Seoul-based regulated Korean commercial bank at which the Yuhan Hoesa will maintain its corporate settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank signatory verified by a licensed Korean notary public followed by a Hague Apostille certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; Apostille path only, consular legalization not used and not chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, signatory, counterparty and its beneficial parents against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions list, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit domestic financial-suspicion watchlist, and Korean criminal-justice PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence is required where any subject is a politically exposed person, family member, known associate, or proxy. Adverse media, corporate registry disqualifications, bankruptcy, tax evasion, trade sanctions, and terrorist-financing red flags must be continuously refreshed for at least 12 months, with a fresh search immediately before each SWIFT LC issuance and wire transfer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (Internet Registration System, www.iros.go.kr) for pre-incorporation name availability and commercial registration search
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the registered trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be expressed in Hangul in a fixed manner. The registration officer applies a four-tier test: (1) mandatory corporate designator denoting limited liability, (2) distinctive Hangul trade name free from confusion with existing registered commercial names, (3) an industry-descriptive element consistent with the registered business scope for battery-grade lithium carbonate wholesale, and (4) a uniqueness layer to avoid identical or deceptively similar names in the same or related business. Phonetic transliteration of overseas parent words is permitted only if represented in Hangul; an English parallel mark may be adopted as an unregistered trade brand but not as the statutory registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of service of the written rejection notice, the applicant, through counsel, must file an immediate appeal with the District Court having jurisdiction over the registration office, attaching the corrected name-search certificate, the amended Articles of Incorporation, and a concise legal memorandum showing compliance with the Korean Commercial Act trade-name rules. The court shall review questions of law and fact; if the appeal is allowed, the registration officer is ordered to complete the registration. In parallel, a fresh incorporating application with a new distinctive trade name may be filed; registration fees already paid will not be refunded unless the appeal succeeds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, mere commercial mailbox, or shared desk address is not acceptable for substantive operation of a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in cross-border procurement, storage, and re-sale of battery-grade lithium carbonate. The National Tax Service requires a fixed place of business evidenced by a genuine lease, a visible business signplate, and actual operating capacity for VAT withholding and customs documentation. Korean banks, applying KOFIU AML customer due diligence rules, will ordinarily refuse to open a corporate account, issue SWIFT documentary credits, or process large wire transfers unless a physical office or bonded warehouse is independently inspected by the account officer. Although the Commercial Registry may formally accept a registered seat at counsel's address, the practical banking and tax posture will be unworkable without physical substance.

stage_1.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) original commercial lease, (2) office signplate and premises photographs, (3) utility invoices and payroll records, (4) corporate VAT filings and customs declarations, (5) procurement warehouse access and inventory records, (6) trade contracts and bill-of-lading files. Likelihood: High for a newly formed mineral-trading company; quantified probability of an unannounced National Tax Service or registry site inspection within the first operating year exceeds 40%, and KOFIU may conduct unpublished on-site AML examinations during the same period.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Part IV Company Law, Chapter IV (Articles 287 through 287-41) governing the Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), together with Articles 288, 289, 292, 295, 302, 317 on incorporation, capital quotas, and registration, and the Commercial Registration Rules of the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, overseen by the Supreme Court of Korea; filings are accepted through the Internet Registration Office (IRO) or in person at the court registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation and Application for Registration of the Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company, resulting in the issuance of a Certificate of Registered Matters from the Commercial Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act. There is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, before registration the founders must fully pay their subscription quotas. Cash contributions must be deposited into a contribution custody account opened in the name of the company to be formed at a Korean commercial bank, and the bank must issue a Certificate of Deposit of Contribution. These funds need not remain blocked after incorporation, but they must be specifically allocated and deposited prior to the registration application. Non-cash contributions require a licensed expert valuation report and must be described in the Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) MADE IN WRITING ON DATE. WHEREAS, the Company is being organized as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea for the purpose of carrying on the cross-border procurement, wholesale trading, and logistics arrangement of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder and related battery metals; WHEREAS, the Company's draft Articles of Incorporation confer management authority upon the directors, permitting decisions to be made by unanimous written resolution; WHEREAS, the founding members have subscribed to the membership quotas set opposite their names in the subscription schedule annexed to the Articles of Incorporation; NOW, THEREFORE, the directors, being all directors entitled to vote, hereby adopt the following resolutions. 1. CONFIRMATION OF SUBSCRIPTION AND INCORPORATION: The directors confirm that each founding member has duly subscribed to the membership quotas of the Company. The total initial membership capital comprising cash contributions has been irrevocably deposited into a contribution custody account at a Korean banking institution chosen by the directors, and the managing director is authorized to collect the bank's deposit certificate and to file the application for incorporation with the competent District Court registry. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the Company shall be established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, which address is located within the territorial jurisdiction of the competent District Court. The managing director is instructed to procure the registered office lease agreement, landlord consent, building owner's verification, and such other physical premise evidence as the registry may require. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Company shall open and maintain corporate operating accounts at a Korean commercial bank and such international banks as may be necessary to support SWIFT letters of credit and wire transfers. The managing director, together with any one other director, shall be the authorized signatories, with each transaction requiring dual signatures above an aggregate threshold of KRW 100,000,000. The directors authorize the issuance of letters of credit, receipt of documentary collections, and execution of foreign exchange transactions consistent with the Company's battery metals arbitrage business. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The directors unanimously appoint NAME to serve as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer with full power to represent the Company; NAME to serve as Director of Operations with responsibility for physical commodity and customs matters; NAME to serve as Director of Finance with responsibility for treasury and bank relations; and NAME to serve as Corporate Secretary responsible for statutory books, minutes, registry filings, and corporate seal management. Because the Company qualifies as a small limited liability company, no statutory auditor is required by law, but the directors nonetheless appoint a compliance officer to manage Foreign Trade Act reporting, chemical import declarations, and AML/KYC obligations. 5. GOVERNMENT FILINGS AND AUTHORIZATION: The Managing Director and the Corporate Secretary are jointly authorized to obtain the Company's corporate seal, to register for tax identification with the National Tax Service, to file the Trade Business Report with the Korea Customs Service, to register the Company's business establishment with local authorities, and to procure any environmental, fire safety, civil defense, or occupational safety clearances required by counsel. 6. INDEMNIFICATION AND EXECUTION: The Company shall indemnify each director and officer to the fullest extent permitted by law for acts reasonably believed to be within the scope of this resolution. This written resolution shall be effective immediately, may be relied upon by third parties, and may be executed in counterparts. CERTIFIED to be a true and complete resolution of the directors of Yuhan Hoesa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Preparation of Draft Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office (IRO) under the Supreme Court of Korea; local Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed company name, Yuhan Hoesa, in the electronic commercial register to verify that no identical or misleadingly similar name exists in the same registry jurisdiction. After securing a clear name search result, prepare the draft Articles of Incorporation with the exact corporate name, registered office address, business purpose covering wholesale of lithium carbonate and battery metals, membership quotas, forms and values of contributions, transfer restrictions, director appointment mechanics, meeting provisions, and initial capital schedule. Submit the draft to a licensed Korean notary for pre-review. The notary will verify the identity and capacity of each founder and confirm that the Articles do not violate mandatory provisions of the Commercial Act. Required dossiers include founder passport or national ID, proof of foreign residential address, draft Articles of Incorporation, membership subscription schedule, and a written statement of the proposed registered office address. The expected turnaround is two business days from receipt of complete documentation. If the court registry objects to the chosen name as identical or misleadingly similar, select the next available name candidate and immediately refile; no administrative appeal is necessary because the registry simply rejects the name and the applicant may reapply without penalty.
required_dossiers: Passport or government-issued ID of each founder
Proof of address or residence of each founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name and refile the same application with corrected name; registry objection may be cured without a hearing. If the notary requests further proof of identity, furnish notarized English translations of passports and additional residence evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Deposit and Issuance of Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank selected as the contribution custody bank, such as a major bank with international banking and trade finance capabilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary contribution custody account in the name of the future company at a Korean bank. Each founder must deposit his or her subscribed capital in KRW through a traceable remittance from the founder's own account. The bank will conduct customer due diligence, politically exposed person screening, and source-of-funds review under the Financial Transactions Reports Act. Upon receipt of the full amount, the bank issues the Certificate of Deposit of Contribution, which is an essential exhibit to the incorporation registration application. If any contribution is made in kind, a licensed appraiser's valuation report must be obtained and the in-kind property must be specifically described in the Articles. The funds should be held in the custody account until the court registration is completed; after incorporation they become available for business operations. The required dossiers include the bank's own account opening forms, founder identification documents, the draft Articles, and a statement of source of funds. The expected turnaround is three business days after receipt of cleared funds. If the bank requests additional AML/CFT documents, provide a corporate group chart, beneficial ownership declaration, trade contract, invoice, and proof of legitimate source of wealth; the bank may extend the timeline to ten business days under enhanced due diligence.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if account is opened through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the deposit due to sanctions or AML review, submit a detailed source-of-wealth explanation and passport and bank statements; if the bank remains unsatisfied, use another bank and restart the deposit process, preserving evidence of the first bank refusal for the registry if needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and Submission of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public licensed by the Ministry of Justice; Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each founder must appear before a Korean notary to declare that the signatures and seals on the Articles are authentic and that the incorporation is not contrary to law. The notary shall notarize the signatures and seal declaration, and the final Articles shall be issued. Thereafter, file the application for registration of incorporation with the Commercial Registration Division of the District Court that has territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. The filing package must include the notarized Articles, the bank deposit certificate, lease agreement and landlord consent for the registered office, identification of the founding members, the membership subscription schedule, and a completed registration form. Registration tax and local education surtax must be paid at the court or through the electronic system. The court will examine the legal permissibility of the business purpose, compliance with the Commercial Act, adequacy of capital evidence, and name uniqueness. The expected turnaround is five business days after a complete filing. If the court issues a supplementary instruction or suspension order, the applicant must respond within seven days by filing a corrective memorandum with supporting documents; if the court denies registration, a new application may be filed after curing the defect without statutory penalty.
required_dossiers: Landlord consent or building owner verification
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For supplementary instructions, prepare a written corrective memorandum and supporting exhibits within seven calendar days. For suspension, request an in-person consultation with the registry judge. For refusal, cure the specific legal defect and resubmit a fresh application; no adverse record attaches to the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration Decision, Certificate Issuance, and Corporate Seal Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court; National Tax Service local district office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registry completes its examination and enters the Company in the commercial register, the court issues a Certified Copy of Corporate Register and a Certificate of Registered Matters. The managing director and corporate secretary must verify that all entries are accurate and then obtain the corporate seal. The corporate seal impression must be reported to the court or applicable administrative office and filed with banks. The Company must also register with the National Tax Service for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and business registration within twenty days of incorporation; the issuance of a Business Registration Certificate is required before banking transactions and customs declarations can be made. The expected turnaround is three business days from court approval to certificate issuance. If the electronic registration certificate is delayed, request an urgent paper certificate from the registry counter. If the tax office challenges the business purpose classification, provide the ISIC 4662 description, a sample sales contract, and proforma invoice to demonstrate that the Company is engaged in wholesale of metal ores and battery materials.
required_dossiers: Court registration approval slip or electronic confirmation
Company corporate seal and seal impression
Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Power of attorney if acting through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certified copy is delayed due to system error, apply for an expedited paper certificate. If the National Tax Service queries the business classification, submit a written explanation of ISIC 4662 wholesale trading activities and supporting trade contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Trade Registration, Bank Account Activation, and Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Customs Service; National Tax Service; the activating bank branch; Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Registered Matters and Business Registration Certificate, file the Trade Business Report under the Foreign Trade Act with the Korea Customs Service, obtain the exporter-importer registration or operator number, and complete importer customs registration. Provide these numbers to the bank to activate the corporate operating account for SWIFT letters of credit and incoming wire transfers. Confirm with the deposit bank that the initial capital is released from custody and available for operations. If lithium carbonate will be imported, the Company must determine whether a chemical substance import declaration under the Chemicals Control Act and its Enforcement Decree applies, and if so, submit the declaration through the Chemicals Information System of the Ministry of Environment. The compliance officer shall maintain the foreign trade ledger, customs manifests, and source documents for five years. The expected turnaround is seven business days from receipt of the registration certificates. If the Korea Customs Service rejects or delays the trade report due to end-user or sanctions concerns, provide an end-user certificate, country of origin data, and the supply contract. If the bank restricts account activation pending further due diligence, submit enhanced KYC information and escalate to the trade finance relationship manager.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Articles of Incorporation
Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC questionnaires
Power of attorney for customs clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Korea Customs Service questions the trade business report, supply end-user certificates and transaction documents. If the bank blocks account activation, provide additional beneficial ownership evidence and, if necessary, open the account with a different licensed Korean bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Korea Customs Service under the Ministry of Strategy and Finance; Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) for foreign trade; Ministry of Environment and local environmental agencies for chemical import and environmental matters; National Fire Agency and local fire departments for civil defense and fire safety
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Export-Import Business Report Certificate and Importer Customs Registration (customs clearance operator number); no statutory manufacturing license applies because the business scope is wholesale procurement and trading of battery-grade lithium carbonate, not production or assembly; however, a chemical substance import declaration may be required for physical imports

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, and its affiliated National Institute of Chemical Safety and local environmental authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category IV Exemption: No Full Environmental Impact Assessment and no Environmental Impact Registration is required for pure wholesale trading and procurement under ISIC 4662. If the Company later operates a warehouse or repacking area, an Environmental Impact Review may be triggered only where the building floor area or storage volume exceeds the thresholds in the Enforcement Decree of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. For now, the Company should file a voluntary self-assessment online and obtain a written clearance confirmation if required by the landlord or bank.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or stack emissions are generated. Domestic sewage must be discharged to the public sewer system and must meet the local municipal sewer ordinances; if any industrial effluent is later generated from sampling or washing, the Clean Water Act effluent limits will apply, specifically BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 30 mg/L, and pH within 5.8-8.6 for discharge to public waters. Air emissions: no point source is expected; if cleaning solvents are introduced, total volatile organic compound emissions must be kept below 10 tons per year to remain below permitting thresholds. Hazardous solid waste, including spent or off-spec lithium carbonate residues, if generated in aggregate above 300 kilograms per month, must be stored in sealed leak-proof containers and transported to a licensed waste treatment facility with manifest records retained for at least five years.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office and any future warehouse must obtain a Basic Firefighting Facility Certificate or temporary fire safety approval from the local fire department before occupancy or customs bonded operations. Evacuation routes, emergency lighting, and fire extinguishers must be installed and inspected in accordance with the Fire Protection and Emergency Management Act. For lithium carbonate dust, a workplace exposure assessment must be conducted by the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency or a certified hygiene laboratory; airborne concentrations should be controlled below the Ministry of Employment and Labor occupational exposure limit for total dust, with appropriate respiratory protection, local exhaust ventilation, and chemical risk assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. The premises must also display civil defense shelter signage and maintain emergency contact and assembly-point protocols in compliance with Korean civil defense obligations for business facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs clearance authority: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS electronic portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC, as a domestic legal entity, must complete its commercial registration with the relevant registry court and, within 20 days of business commencement, file an Application for Business Registration (Business Registration Certificate application) with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over its registered seat, or electronically through HomeTax. Attachments include certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, notice of business commencement, lease agreement or title evidence for the registered seat, proof of Korean bank account, registered director/shareholder identification, and authorization letter for the preparation agent. The NTS then issues a Business Registration Certificate with a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as both the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number and the Korean VAT registration number. If the entity is approached as a foreign non-resident business operator with no fixed domestic place of business, the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative and file the simplified non-resident business registration via HomeTax; the tax representative submits the foreign certificate of incorporation, charter, passport, power of attorney, and evidence of Korean taxable supplies. No alternative federal entity election is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None — the Korean tax system does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election. A Yuhan Hoesa LLC is automatically classified as a Korean domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income; hybrid mismatch rules in the Adjustment of International Tax Act override any secondary statutory election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act (Republic of Korea).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold; any person supplying goods or services in Korea in the course of business is required to register as a VAT business operator from the commencement of business. The simplified taxpayer threshold of KRW 80 million annual turnover applies only to very small resident individual traders and cannot be used by a Yuhan Hoesa LLC to avoid standard VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Korean mandatory e-invoicing regime requires all registered VAT businesses to issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice) through the National Tax Service HomeTax system. E-tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following issuance through the integrated e-invoice API system, allowing real-time data validation and automatic reconciliation with customs declarations in UNI-PASS. There is no separate crypto-tax stamping window; anti-fraud digital control is achieved through mandatory e-invoice central registration, continuous NTS system monitoring, and invoice-return matching on VAT returns. Export supplies must be documented with a zero-rated e-tax invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export VAT treatment is available for battery-grade lithium carbonate powder physically exported from Korea to a foreign destination under the Value-Added Tax Act. The Yuhan Hoesa must prove: (i) the goods were delivered into the Korean export customs channel through Korea Customs Service; (ii) sale to a foreign purchaser; (iii) the goods left Korean territory and customs territory; (iv) the settlement amount in foreign currency was deposited in a bank account; and (v) the export documents are retained for the statutory period. Qualifying digital services supplied to foreign users for consumption outside Korea may also be zero-rated if the supplier holds evidence of foreign user status, foreign use, and foreign currency payment; supply of such services to Korean recipients remains taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration) accepted by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading (B/L) issued by the ocean carrier evidencing the lithium cargo shipped from Korea to the foreign consignee
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation issued by a Korean bank demonstrating receipt of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service will audit export zero-rating substantiation and may use UNI-PASS and bank exchange transaction data to verify actual shipment and repatriation. If the export documents are false, the goods do not leave Korea, or the foreign exchange proceeds are not received within the prescribed period, the zero-rating is retrospectively cancelled: VAT becomes due at the standard 10% rate, the exporter must file an amended VAT return, any refund previously credited is clawed back with penalty tax surcharges (up to 40% of the underpaid VAT, plus interest), and criminal liability may be pursued under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for fraudulent evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (Central Bank), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with delegated banking supervisory execution through the Financial Supervisory Service and policy coordination with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for genuine current account transactions such as trade payments, operational expenses, and profit repatriation, but every inbound and outbound remittance must pass through an authorized foreign exchange bank and be reported in the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Capital account transactions, including shareholder capital contributions, foreign loans, equity subscription proceeds, and long-term debt instruments, are also permitted for foreign-invested companies, but they require a prior report or a registration certificate issued by the designated foreign exchange bank. The key operational hurdle is not a prohibition on convertibility but the documentary discipline: banks require the underlying trade contract, customs declaration, tax invoice, and correct foreign exchange purpose code, and they have a statutory duty to reject any remittance with inconsistent or incomplete supporting papers. For profit remittance, the entity must prove distributable profits via audited Korean IFRS financial statements and a board resolution, then deduct 22% corporate income tax and 10% dividend withholding tax, subject to treaty relief where available; only the after-tax dividend is freely convertible and can be sent through the bank as long as the dividend-related tax has been paid. In practice, for a battery-metals arbitrage company, the Bank of Korea and Financial Supervisory Service will also review actual commodity trade flows and may request evidence that the lithium carbonate imports are not a disguised speculative carry trade or layered transfer-pricing mechanism.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 5-2 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, an exporter must collect its export proceeds within six months of the export declaration date and must deposit them into a foreign-currency deposit account at a licensed foreign exchange bank. The mandatory conversion ratio to Korean won is 0% for current export proceeds; the company may retain the proceeds in USD or other major currencies indefinitely for working capital, supplier settlement, or treasury hedging purposes. If the six-month collection deadline is missed, the exporter must file a delayed-receipt report through the managing bank with a written justification, and the Bank of Korea may order a settlement or impose administrative sanctions. Compliance requires reconciliation of the export customs declaration, the inward credit notice, and the FEIS transaction report within the prescribed window.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD multi-currency)
Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account plus Foreign Currency Trade Settlement Account
Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Deposit Account and KRW Operating Account
Capital Escrow Account and Legacy International Banking Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. South Korean statutory banking regulations require every corporate foreign exchange transaction to be conducted through a bank licensed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Offshore financial technology entities such as Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, or Currencycloud are not authorized foreign exchange banks in South Korea; they cannot issue a domestic KRW account number, cannot legally receive or disburse KRW, and cannot perform the mandatory FEIS reporting. They may only serve as an ancillary payment corridor for funds already converted through an authorized Korean bank, and even then, the final remittance must be executed through the licensed banks. For a medium-risk battery-metals trader handling million-dollar import settlements, reliance on an offshore digital EMI would create unrepairable compliance gaps, delay customs clearance, and compromise the auditor's capital verification process. The Korean receiving bank may also reject inbound wires from non-bank fintech accounts because the ultimate ordering customer does not satisfy the identity verification and financial information reporting requirements. Consequently, the treasury blueprint must use only tier-1 Korean commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance at a domestic branch remains the default statutory mandate for a foreign director of a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. The bank must verify the director's identity in compliance with the Financial Transactions Reporting Act and the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. Remote video identification is accepted only for registered aliens holding a valid Alien Registration Card with an existing domestic financial transaction record. A consular proxy opening is not recognized by any major Korean commercial bank as sufficient evidence for the corporate KYC interview. The representative director, or a Korean-resident director with a board resolution and notarized power of attorney, must appear at a domestic branch to sign the corporate signature card, deposit seal declaration, specimen signature, and internal AML interview questionnaire. If the foreign director is outside Korea, the practical alternative is to appoint a second domestic resident director to attend in person while the foreign director's identity is separately verified using a notarized and apostilled passport, articles of incorporation, and beneficial ownership declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership resides in a non-resident corporate parent registered in a buy-side intermediary jurisdiction, creating a clear ownership chain disclosure failure under Korean Financial Transactions Reporting Act beneficial ownership rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed KOFIU beneficial ownership disclosure form, apostilled certificate of incumbency for the parent entity, a full organizational chart covering all intermediate holding vehicles, tax residence certificates for each entity, passport copies of ultimate natural persons, and a sworn statement confirming no shell company or FATF-listed jurisdiction is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid initial capitalization through a shareholder loan from a foreign affiliate triggers suspicion of disguised financing and reverse money laundering, especially where the new Korean entity has no prior operating ledger.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Korean-translated, notarized loan agreement; 12 months of original bank statements and tax filings proving the lender's source of funds; a board resolution approving the loan terms; a Foreign Exchange Transactions Act loan report stamped by the authorized foreign exchange bank; and a three-year business plan demonstrating that the loan will be deployed solely for lithium carbonate procurement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicator caused by inconsistent pricing against the benchmark for battery-grade lithium carbonate when shipments are routed through a third-party trading hub such as Hong Kong or Singapore rather than the origin point to Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contract with a pricing formula referencing Argus, Fastmarkets, or LME battery-grade lithium carbonate averages; independent pre-shipment inspection certificate from SGS, Bureau Veritas, or Intertek confirming commodity purity and volume; full transport document package including bill of lading, freight invoice, packing list, countries of origin certificates; and an internationally prepared transfer pricing benchmarking report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound wire for foreign equity capital arrives from an account name that differs from the registered foreign-investor name, creating a third-party payment mismatch in the FEIS system and a suspicion of impersonation or structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment remitter authorization deed, corporate resolution of the registered investor appointing the third party as paying agent, signed passport and corporate registration of the remitter, and legal ownership evidence demonstrating that the remitter is a wholly owned subsidiary or an appointed paying agent of the registered investor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a foreign-invested Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the compliant routing is as follows: the foreign shareholder must submit a Foreign Investment Report through a designated domestic bank or KOTRA, receive the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, and then remit capital by SWIFT MT103 into the dedicated Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account under the entity name. The remittance must be declared through the authorized foreign exchange bank and entered into the FEIS with the precise foreign exchange purpose code corresponding to foreign direct investment in wholesale trade of minerals and battery materials. The bank will verify that the fund remitter matches the registered investor, that the beneficial ownership KYC file is complete, and that the remittance narrative references the underlying Korean entity and planned ISIC 4662 business activity. After crediting, a licensed Korean certified public accountant must issue a capital contribution verification report before the funds are released from escrow into the company's basic operating account. Any mismatch between the remitter name, the FEIS declaration, and the foreign investment report will suspend the release and require an amended declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All supplier payments for battery-grade lithium carbonate import settlement should run through a licensed Korean bank using one of four clearing rails: direct SWIFT MT103 wires with a full narrative referencing the invoice, packing list, and bill of lading; irrevocable commercial letters of credit (LC) recommended for high-value shipments above USD 250,000; documentary collections for established long-term suppliers; or open-account settlement for low-risk jurisdictions. Every disbursement requires a foreign exchange transaction report in FEIS and the presentation of the Korean importer's customs import declaration. The bank will verify the underlying purchase order, the commercial invoice, the bill of lading date, the vessel or air waybill, and the country-of-origin certificate to screen sanctions exposure and trade-based money laundering patterns. For recurring supplier payments, a standing payment mandate with pre-approved transaction thresholds can be established to expedite clearing while maintaining full audit trail compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/KRW forward contracts with an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank, executed at or below 100% of real import exposure and requiring presentation of underlying lithium carbonate purchase contracts.

Cross-currency swaps between KRW and USD for long-term battery materials procurement financing, permitted only when notional exposure is justified by committed purchase orders and maturities do not exceed the underlying trade cycle.

Option-based hedging strategies including zero-premium USD/KRW collars, permissible through Korean investment-grade banks, provided positions are fair-valued under K-IFRS and do not create a speculative open position.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for Korean resident corporate treasury hedging; offshore NDF referencing is treated as an unregistered foreign exchange transaction and is prohibited by the Bank of Korea, therefore all hedging must be delivered, settled, and booked onshore.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary meeting of members and approval of separate annual financial statements, including the balance sheet, income statement, and appropriation of retained earnings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate governance records of the Yuhan Hoesa; no government filing at the meeting level, but the approved financial statements must be submitted to the National Tax Service and, if externally audited, reported to the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the ordinary meeting does not create an automatic administrative strike-off, but blocks lawful dividend distributions and prevents timely completion of the corporate tax return; continued failure together with tax non-filing exposes the company to National Tax Service seizure, business-registration cancellation, and court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Domestic corporate income tax return, tax adjustment schedule, and payment; local income tax surtax of ten percent (10%) of corporate income tax is paid with the same return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (central corporate income tax) and the competent local government of the registered office (local income tax surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end; calendar-year company: March 31; an additional one-month extension is available when filed through a licensed tax accountant or certified public accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underreporting penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes of up to 10%-40% of unpaid tax depending on negligence or fraud; per-diem delinquency interest currently 0.022% accrues on unpaid amounts; enforced collection, seizure of assets, cancellation of business registration, and potential court-ordered dissolution for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax returns: interim returns for the first and third quarters and final returns for the first and second six-month periods, including export/zero-rated invoices for cross-border battery-grade lithium carbonate sales and purchase invoices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through the competent district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25, April 25, July 25, and October 25 of each calendar year for the relevant supply periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of ten percent (10%) of the unpaid or underdeclared VAT amount; per-diem delinquency interest on arrears; denial of input VAT credits if tax invoices are not issued or received correctly; business premises closure and collection measures for severe non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent external audit report and audited financial statements, including appointment of a certified public accountant and submission/reporting of the audit report with the statutory authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent CPA/accounting firm; National Tax Service; Financial Supervisory Service and Securities and Futures Commission for audit-mandated companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, in time for the ordinary members' meeting within three (3) months after fiscal year-end; audited statements are attached to the corporate tax return due by March 31 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to undergo a mandatory statutory audit is treated as defective statutory filing: the Financial Services Commission may designate an external auditor, impose administrative sanctions and fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, and the audited financial statements may be disregarded for tax purposes, causing reassessment, additional tax penalties, and interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment follow-up report and share-transfer notification for non-resident shareholders/investors (applicable where the Yuhan Hoesa is a foreign-invested company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within thirty (30) days after any triggering event, including a share transfer, capital increase/decrease, change of foreign investor nationality, or change of foreign investment ratio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the prescribed foreign-investment change report may trigger administrative penalties under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; it may also jeopardize foreign-investor tax incentive status, dividend repatriation protection, and foreign-investment eligibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Overseas financial account report (foreign bank account, securities, derivatives, and cash-value insurance) if the aggregate year-end or maximum balance exceeds the statutory threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (overseas financial account filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By June 30 of the year following the reporting calendar year; applies where foreign financial account balances exceed KRW 500 million at any point during the reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported or underreported foreign account balances are subject to additional tax up to 20% of the unreported amount or KRW 20 million for non-filing, with higher criminal penalties for amounts exceeding KRW 5 billion; no automatic corporate strike-off, but continued non-compliance elevates AML and tax-crime risk

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to obtain an independent CPA audit if its total assets at fiscal year-end are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million). The threshold is balance-sheet-based; there is no independent turnover or employee-headcount trigger under the Korean external-audit law. Additionally, the Financial Services Commission may designate a company with total assets of KRW 5 billion or more as audit-mandated when public interest or investor protection requires it, and any company that has issued or listed securities is audited regardless of asset size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for audit-mandated/public-interest companies or under Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for non-public companies that do not adopt K-IFRS. The audit itself is performed under Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), and the corporate income tax return is prepared by adding a Korean tax-adjustment schedule to the accounting-based profit or loss.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a general annual beneficial-ownership confirmation return or public UBO register for ordinary Yuhan Hoesa companies. However, for a foreign-invested company, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires the company and its foreign investors to file an investment-change report within thirty (30) days of any share transfer or change in foreign-investor identity/ratio. Financial institutions under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information perform customer due diligence and beneficial-owner verification at account opening and on an event-driven risk-refresh basis; this is not an annual company-registry filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, evidencing each member's ownership and transfer history
Register of Directors or equivalent management/officer registration record, where a management organ is constituted
Register of Charges or mortgages over company assets and any prescribed security registrations
Minute Book containing annual and extraordinary members' meetings and, if applicable, board of directors' meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 2,500 per year for a standard Korean registered office and corporate secretarial agent, depending on location and service scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 to USD 45,000 per year for a certified statutory audit of a trading company subject to mandatory external audit; for a company below the audit threshold, an accountant-compiled financial statement and tax package typically ranges from USD 3,000 to USD 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; 19% on the next KRW 200 million; 21% on the next KRW 200 million; 24% on the next KRW 200 million; 27% on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion (progressive rates for fiscal year 2024, plus 10% surtax on corporate tax for taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays for high-tech foreign-invested enterprises; Free Economic Zone (FEZ) and Foreign Investment Zone corporate tax reductions of 50-100% for 3-5 years; Special Taxation Restriction Act R&D tax credits (up to 30-40% of qualifying R&D expenditures); patent box regime (increased deduction for qualifying intellectual property income up to 5% of qualifying IP income); no dedicated offshore patent box but IP exploitation via domestic entity qualifies for R&D and technology transfer income deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean corporate income tax return Form No. 40 (법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서) filed via HomeTax System (홈택스) electronic portal; supplementary schedules include Form No. 40-1 (tax base and computation), Form No. 40-2 (adjustment entries), and transfer pricing disclosure Form No. 40-3 (List of International Transactions with Special Related Persons)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with mandatory semi-annual interim tax prepayments for corporations with prior-year taxable income exceeding KRW 5 million)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (by March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers; for fiscal year ending December 31, 2025, filing deadline is March 31, 2026); interim prepayment returns due within 2 months after the first 6 months of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year beginning and ending dates for the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the fiscal year period exactly as registered with the Korean tax office. A non-resident parent or foreign shareholder must ensure the Korean entity's fiscal year is consistently aligned with the economic substance of cross-border procurement transactions, and any change of fiscal year requires prior approval from the District Tax Office to avoid deemed income determination under Article 66 of the Corporate Income Tax Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, business registration number, address, and representative director information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the Korean entity's exact registered name (Yuhan Hoesa) and its domestic representative. If the actual decision-maker is a foreign director or expatriate manager, the return must still list the registered domestic representative; failure to disclose a foreign de facto manager may constitute inaccurate return filing and trigger personal liability of the domestic representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base after adding back non-deductible expenses and applying loss carryforwards and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a battery-grade lithium carbonate procurement arbitrage entity, include all cross-border trading margins in Korean-source taxable income unless a permanent establishment (PE) determination applies. Deductions for intercompany purchases must satisfy arm's length pricing under Article 4 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA); non-deductible foreign income taxes may be claimed as a foreign tax credit only if the foreign tax was paid on Korean-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits including foreign tax credits, R&D credits, and employment creation credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder with a Korean procurement entity cannot claim direct R&D credits unless the underlying R&D activity is performed in Korea. Foreign tax credits are limited to the lesser of Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income or the actual foreign tax paid; documentation must include certified foreign tax returns and translated assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, interim tax prepayments, and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter prepayments made during the year, including any withholding tax withheld by Korean counterparties on interest or royalty income. If the entity has a qualified PE, non-resident branch tax under Article 95 of the Corporate Income Tax Law may be required on the after-tax income attributable to the Korean business; the branch tax return must be filed within 3 months of fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable after deductions, reductions, and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that all transfer pricing adjustments (including cost of goods sold adjustments for lithium carbonate procurement) are reflected before final determination. A non-resident parent entity must not cause the Korean subsidiary to report a loss while the overall cross-border supply chain earns high profits, as this triggers the tax avoidance provisions under Article 4(3) of the LCITA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 0.03% per day of the unpaid tax, up to a maximum of 7.5%; unfaithful return penalty of 20% of the underreported corporate tax amount; failure to pay tax penalty of 0.022% per day of unpaid amount; criminal prosecution for fraudulent returns under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to KRW 20 million (or up to 5 years imprisonment and KRW 50 million for aggravated tax evasion exceeding KRW 300 million).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 20% (including 2% local income surtax) for outbound dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; 10% (including 1% local surtax) for outbound interest and royalty income under the Corporate Income Tax Law
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must submit (1) a Korea Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the residence country, (2) Form 40-3 international transaction disclosure and the Application for Reduction/Exemption of Withholding Tax under the tax treaty (외국법인 국내원천소득에 대한 법인세 면제·경감 신청서), (3) a Beneficial Ownership Certificate and supporting economic substance evidence, (4) proof no offshore routing is used for treaty shopping, and (5) the Korean withholding agent files the treaty relief application with the District Tax Office prior to payment. Korea applies the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clause in treaties where applicable; if the DTA rate is lower than the statutory rate, the reduced rate applies only upon submission of the TRC in original form with apostille or consular legalization, plus Korean translation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest paid to non-residents: 22% (20% corporate tax plus 2% local surtax) for royalty income; 22% (20% plus 2% local surtax) for interest income; treaty rate under the Korea-US DTA is 15% for royalties and 10% for interest (with 1% local surtax applied treaty-wide); under the Korea-China DTA, 10% for royalties and 10% for interest; treaty relief requires full beneficial ownership and documentation of the licensing or debt structure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File required if aggregate intercompany transactions exceed KRW 100 billion in the fiscal year; Local File required if intercompany transactions with a foreign related party exceed KRW 5 billion per year; for a lithium carbonate procurement arbitrage entity, intercompany cross-border purchases or sales exceeding KRW 1 billion also trigger contemporaneous TP documentation requirement under the LCITA.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) do not apply in Korea as a standalone statutory regime, but a Korean limited liability company engaged in cross-border lithium carbonate procurement must demonstrate real business substance to avoid PE characterization, CFC attribution, and treaty abuse challenges. The Korean tax authorities apply the Substance-over-Form doctrine under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) under Article 4 of the LCITA. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are procurement contract negotiation, purchase order execution, quality inspection, logistics coordination, and pricing decisions. If these CIGA are performed offshore by a foreign parent while the Korean entity is a pure shell, the Korean entity may be subject to penalty adjustments and the foreign parent may be deemed to have a Korean PE through the subsidiary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion through Transfer Pricing Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially inflated cost of imported battery-grade lithium carbonate from a Hong Kong or Swiss related party, or selling at a discount to a foreign affiliate, resulting in a sustained Korean operating loss while the group earns a premium margin; failure to prepare or submit contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for intercompany transactions above KRW 1 billion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 4 (Adjustment of Tax Base) and Article 10 (Penalty Tax) of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA): unfaithful filing penalty of 20% of the additional corporate tax assessed, and penalty tax up to 30% for inadequate TP documentation. Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 2 years and a fine up to KRW 20 million; aggravated evasion exceeding KRW 300 million carries up to 5 years imprisonment and a fine up to KRW 50 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Commercial Act: a representative director who intentionally or negligently caused the tax evasion is joint and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and additional charges. Directors may face travel restrictions and blacklisting by the National Tax Service (NTS) for unpaid taxes exceeding KRW 50 million; criminal conviction results in imprisonment, and civil asset restitution may be enforced against personal property of the director if corporate assets insufficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of Yuhan Hoesa as a pure Dutch-boy conduit without physical office, staff, warehouse, or procurement management functions; all substantive decisions and CIGA performed by the foreign parent; using the Korean entity solely for treaty-shopping benefits to obtain a reduced withholding tax rate on dividends or trading profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under Articles 90-91 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and anti-treaty-shopping provisions in Korea's DTAs; the NTS may recharacterize the shell as a mere agency of the foreign parent and assess corporate tax at 22-27% plus branch tax at 22% on the deemed distributable income. Administrative penalty of 30% of the understated tax under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; criminal sanctions for fraud under Article 347 of the Criminal Act if intentional concealment of transactions is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell entity who sign false purchase orders, issue inflated invoices, or submit incorrect returns may be held criminally liable as co-principals. The Commercial Act imposes liability on directors for damage caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct, allowing creditors or the NTS to attach director personal assets. Foreign directors residing in Korea may be subject to departure bans, while non-resident directors may be individually pursued through Mutual Assistance procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Outbound Profit Repatriation and Dividend WHT Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Avoiding Korean dividend withholding tax by disguising dividends as inflated service fees, management fees, or interest payments to a foreign parent; failing to file the international transaction disclosure form (Form 40-3); using an offshore intermediary jurisdiction (e.g., BVI, Hong Kong, or Singapore) with no economic substance to route outbound remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax recharacterization under Article 93 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and Article 6 of the LCITA: the disguised fee is reclassified as a constructive dividend and subjected to 20% (22% with local surtax) withholding tax plus a 10% (of the additional tax) unfaithful return penalty and 0.03% daily late payment penalty. Article 31 of the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes penalty surcharges up to 80% of the additional tax where fraudulent intentional revenue concealment is verified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the fake service fee structure have personal secondary liability for the unpaid WHT under Article 42 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 401 of the Commercial Act. Criminal prosecution may occur for intentional evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, leading to imprisonment up to 5 years, fines, and asset seizure. The NTS may register the directors on the hard-core delinquent taxpayer public disclosure list for cumulative evasion exceeding KRW 50 million, severely impairing credit, travel, and business operations.
